fact_text: Four of Pakistan's five refineries together earned about PKR 57 billion profit in Q1 FY27 (July to September 2026), as reported in the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The same four refineries earned only about PKR 2.9 billion profit in the corresponding quarter a year earlier, the video reports.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Pakistan's refineries run only on imported crude, because the older hydro-skimming plants cannot process local heavy crude such as Thar or Sindh oil.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Because of the old refinery setup, Pakistan imports large volumes of petrol while exporting leftover furnace oil, the reverse of the efficient product balance.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The pump price of fuel is built up from the refinery ex-refinery base price, then oil marketing company and dealer margins, then taxes and duties added on top.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The petroleum levy charged per litre at the pump has become a major source of government revenue, so the petrol pump works as a tax collection point.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: On 30 Oct 2026 the federal cabinet froze the petrol ex-refinery price for 30 days at the 7 March 2026 pre-war level, removing extra spreads, premiums and incidental costs that rose during the Iran-US war.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Under the new petrol formula the import cost is fixed at the March 2026 price, and refineries must deposit the gap between import price and the fixed ex-refinery price into the petroleum levy account.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Refinery operators say the petrol price change was made without consulting them, and that sudden policy shifts damage refinery balance sheets and deter investment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Refinery operators argue the construction duty was meant to flow into a project pool that funds their upgrade, but the government instead put that money into petroleum levies.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Pakistan's refinery upgrade programme needs about USD 6 billion of investment in total, the video reports.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: On 24 Sep 2026 four major refineries signed upgrade agreements worth five to six billion US dollars under the government's upgrade policy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The upgrade plans are expected to raise petrol production by up to 72 percent, as stated in the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The upgrade plans are expected to raise diesel output by about 39 percent, as stated in the video.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The upgrade plans are expected to cut furnace oil output by about 63 percent, as the video says, because the refineries would convert it into lighter fuels.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The government estimates that each year of delay in refinery upgrade agreements costs the economy about USD 1.5 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: In the 2024 budget petroleum products were exempted from sales tax just as refineries were signing an upgrade agreement, and the issue took about two years to correct by amendment.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Refinery operators say they could not recover the sales tax paid on inputs because their product prices were fixed, which kept the problem open for about two years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: Refinery operators asked the government to keep policy consistent, to avoid abrupt changes, and to consult them first when pressure arises, as was done in the earlier diesel case.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)

fact_text: The reporter argued that abrupt, irrational policy changes make any investor weigh a Pakistan refinery project very carefully before committing money.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Fuel Price Policy: Is Refinery Investment at Risk? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-11-12)
